newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Mortar bomb explosion reported in divided Mostar.
newsitem.headline: Mortar bomb explosion reported in divided Mostar.

text.p: The NATO-led peace force said on Saturday it was investigating a mortar bomb explosion in the divided Bosnian town of Mostar amid rising tensions between rival Moslem and Croat communities.

The Stabilisation Force (SFOR) said it was examining evidence to determine whether two 60mm mortar bombs were fired in the town or if one was detonated without having been fired, SFOR spokesman Major Andrew Saddleton said.
"We are investigating whether they were actually fired," Saddleton told Reuters. "There are other ways to get a mortar bomb to detonate."
An officer with the International Police Task Force in Mostar reported earlier that one mortar bomb struck a house in Moslem-held eastern quarter and a second bomb did not explode.
There were no injuries reported from the explosion which occurred at 1:20 a.m. on Saturday near the Carinski bridge in the town centre.

There were also conflicting reports about where the mortar bomb explosion occurred. IPTF said the mortar bombs hit the east side of Mostar while SFOR reported the explosions occurred on the Croat-controlled west side.
The mortar bomb blasts represented a grave violation of the Dayton peace accord, which requires "heavy" weapons to be registered at designated storage sites.
Sporadic gunfire and several smaller explosions, suspected to be hand grenades, were also heard overnight, SFOR spokesmen said.
The report comes after serious violence erupted in Mostar last Monday.
Armed Croat men opened fire on a procession of Moslems trying to visit a cemetery in the Croat-controlled western sector. One man was shot dead and at least 22 were wounded.

Croat and Moslem leaders agreed to defuse tensions in an agreement brokered by international envoys two days later. But human rights workers say Croat thugs have been expelling the remaining Moslems in western Mostar since Monday's clash.
